governance_note: New or changed online regulatory content must NOT automatically overwrite entries here. Changes require an impact assessment and quality approval (approval_status must be APPROVED before a rule may drive decisions).

entries.document: GVP Module VI Rev 2 (EMA/873138/2011 Rev 2), VI.B.2
entries.requirement_interpretation: A valid ICSR requires four minimum criteria: identifiable reporter, identifiable patient, at least one suspected medicinal product, at least one suspected adverse reaction.
entries.implementation_rule: ICSR minimum-criteria check; missing criteria drive follow-up questions and validity flag.

entries.requirement_interpretation: Serious ICSRs: expedited submission no later than 15 calendar days from receipt. Non-serious EEA ICSRs: 90 calendar days.
entries.implementation_rule: Reporting urgency input to question prioritisation.

entries.document: GVP Module VI Addendum I (EMA/405655/2016) - Duplicate management of suspected adverse reaction reports
entries.requirement_interpretation: Confirmed duplicates are merged under a master case (allocated or newly created). Subordinate cases remain in the database for audit trail and follow-up receipt, flagged as duplicates and linked to the master; subordinate identifiers are recorded in E2B(R3) C.1.9.1. Only the master is used for signal detection and medical evaluation. Receipt of new information triggers a new duplicate check. Same-sender duplicates: sender is notified; one case nullified and remaining case updated as follow-up.
entries.implementation_rule: Reversible master-case merge with subordinate linkage, audit trail, re-check on new information.

entries.document: GVP Module VI Addendum II - ICSR personal data protection / masking policy
entries.requirement_interpretation: Personal data in ICSR fields submitted to EudraVigilance must be masked or left blank per the common masking policy.
entries.implementation_rule: No request or storage of unnecessary direct identifiers in outbound questionnaires.

entries.document: ICH E2D(R1) Post-Approval Safety Data Management, Section 6.4 (follow-up) and 6.6 (duplicate management), Section 4.5 (literature)
entries.version: Step 4 final (adopted 2025-08-19); EU effective 2026-03-18; Health Canada implemented 2026-01-12
entries.requirement_interpretation: MAHs should seek follow-up information to allow scientific evaluation, prioritising significant/serious cases; follow-up is documented and new information is managed as a follow-up report. Literature articles describing a pre-existing case are added to that case (citation + medical detail) and reported as follow-up as appropriate; duplicate detection applies when literature cases may have been reported by other means.
entries.implementation_rule: Gap-driven question generation with documented attempts; literature-to-case linkage classification FOLLOWUP_TO_EXISTING_ICSR.

entries.document: ICH E2B(R3) ICSR Implementation Guide, G.k.8 Action(s) Taken with Drug (OID 2.16.840.1.113883.3.989.2.1.1.15)
entries.requirement_interpretation: G.k.8 allowed values: 1=Drug withdrawn, 2=Dose reduced, 3=Dose increased, 4=Dose not changed, 0=Unknown, 9=Not applicable. 'Not applicable' covers e.g. patient died, treatment completed before reaction/event, or characterisation of drug role = Drug Not Administered. One action per G.k instance; relevant time anchor is the reaction/event onset.
entries.implementation_rule: E2B code mapping table E2B_GK8; not-applicable preconditions enforced.

entries.document: ICH E2B(R3) ICSR Implementation Guide, G.k.8 + E.i.7 user guidance
entries.requirement_interpretation: E2B(R3) has no standalone dechallenge data element: G.k.8 value 1 (Drug withdrawn) taken together with E.i.7 (Outcome of Reaction/Event at Time of Last Observation: 1=recovered/resolved, 2=recovering/resolving, 3=not recovered/not resolved, 4=recovered/resolved with sequelae, 5=fatal, 0=unknown) describes the dechallenge.
entries.implementation_rule: Dechallenge derived from action + outcome per drug-event pair; never invented as a separate E2B value.

entries.document: ICH E2B(R3) ICSR Implementation Guide, G.k.9.i.4 Did Reaction Recur on Re-administration? (OID 2.16.840.1.113883.3.989.2.1.1.16)
entries.requirement_interpretation: G.k.9.i.4 allowed values: 1=yes-yes (rechallenge done, reaction recurred), 2=yes-no (done, did not recur), 3=yes-unk (done, outcome unknown), 4=no-n/a (no rechallenge done).
entries.implementation_rule: E2B code mapping E2B_GK9I4; positive requires documented re-administration plus supported recurrence.

entries.document: 21 CFR 314.80 (drugs) / 21 CFR 600.80 (biologics) - Postmarketing reporting of adverse experiences
entries.requirement_interpretation: 15-day Alert reports for adverse experiences that are both serious and unexpected, from initial receipt (Day 0). Follow-up reports within 15 calendar days of new information. Literature-based 15-day reports must be accompanied by a copy of the article. Minimum reportable information: identifiable patient, identifiable reporter, suspect product, adverse experience.
entries.implementation_rule: Urgency scoring for serious+unexpected; literature flag requires full-text acquisition for submission copy.

entries.document: Federal Register notice 2026-06660: Electronic submission of postmarketing ICSRs to FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS, formerly FAERS) using ICH E2B(R3)
entries.requirement_interpretation: Beginning 2026-10-01, postmarketing ICSRs for human drugs/biologics/drug-led combination products submitted via ESG NextGen must use ICH E2B(R3) data standards to the AEMS database.
entries.implementation_rule: E2B(R3) field coding is authoritative for US submissions from the effective date.

entries.requirement_interpretation: MedDRA 29.0 is the current terminology version. MedDRA is licence-restricted: no MedDRA content may be embedded in this package. Coding outputs must be validated against a licensed MedDRA installation in the deployment environment. The bundled mini-lexicon in nexus_agents/terminology.py is a development placeholder ONLY and must be replaced by licensed terminology services before clinical use.
entries.implementation_rule: Terminology service interface with placeholder implementation; coding completeness flagged UNCODED when the licensed service is unavailable.

entries.document: GVP Module IX Rev 1 (EMA/827661/2011 Rev 1) - Signal management
entries.requirement_interpretation: Duplicate cases can inflate or mask signals; signal-relevant literature should be routed for signal assessment even when not an individual case.
entries.implementation_rule: Signal-relevance flag independent of ICSR inclusion decision.
